cases.scenario: A small request has one clear output and one write surface.
invariants: The Graph skill does not trigger.
No control plane or delegated Agent is created.

cases.scenario: The user asks only for a Graph plan for a complex task.
invariants: The validated plan and Dashboard are delivered.
No Worker, Validator, target mutation, or business external effect occurs.

cases.scenario: The initial request asks to complete a complex goal but no generated plan exists yet.
invariants: The Planner compiles and displays the plan.
Execution stops in awaiting_user_approval until the exact version is approved.

cases.scenario: Approval names a different plan version or hash.
invariants: The approval is rejected.
No Node becomes active.

cases.scenario: A role, Node, Edge, Task, Artifact, scope, effect, exception, or approved capacity is materially changed.
invariants: The plan version and hash change.
Approval is invalidated and the revised Graph is shown again.

cases.scenario: Every Node depends on the previous Node.
invariants: Each topological wave contains one Node.
Downstream remains blocked until its predecessor is accepted.

cases.scenario: Two Nodes have accepted inputs and disjoint scopes.
invariants: They may enter the same wave within effective capacity.
Parallel execution is not claimed before both actually launch.

cases.scenario: A Node fans out to two independent Nodes which feed a join.
invariants: The middle Nodes may run together.
The join remains blocked until all required inputs are accepted.

cases.scenario: Runtime or permission capacity differs from the hard maximum.
invariants: Capacity equals min(15, runtime, permission).
Coordinator, Workers, and Validators count; the Dashboard does not.

cases.scenario: The host capacity cannot be verified.
invariants: The plan does not assume 15 slots.
Work is serialized or the limitation is reported.

cases.scenario: Two otherwise ready Nodes own overlapping write or external-effect scopes.
invariants: They do not run concurrently.
The Graph adds a dependency or fails compilation.

cases.scenario: A Graph Node lacks a Task or a Task is shared by Nodes.
invariants: Compilation fails.
Reported Node and Task counts are derived from complete contracts.

cases.scenario: A Node has missing, not-run, or failing test/lint evidence.
invariants: The Node cannot be submitted or accepted.
No downstream Artifact is released.

cases.scenario: A conventional test or lint is inapplicable.
invariants: The equivalent check, reason, steps, condition, and evidence appear before approval.
The executor cannot create an unapproved exception.

cases.scenario: A Validator brief contains implementer narrative, rationale, steering, or expected conclusions.
invariants: The brief is rejected.
Only feature/module facts, references, and reproducible steps are accepted.

cases.scenario: A Validator only replays planned conformance tests and declares no independent boundary invariant.
invariants: Compilation rejects the empty boundary-check set.
Applicable precision, overflow, ordering, determinism, equivalence, resource, or security boundaries are exercised with independently generated inputs.

cases.scenario: The proposed Validator implemented an Artifact under test or attempts to modify it.
invariants: Independent validation cannot be accepted.
Repairs are routed through the Coordinator.

cases.scenario: An accepted upstream Artifact version or digest changes after dependent work.
invariants: Transitive dependents become stale.
Affected active work is isolated and revalidated with a new attempt.

cases.scenario: The control plane starts its HTTP Dashboard.
invariants: It binds 127.0.0.1 on default port 8088 or an explicit port.
It provides no authentication, TLS, remote bind, or write API.

cases.scenario: Task, Artifact, Registry, or revision files change atomically.
invariants: The Dashboard refreshes from landed state and emits a revision event.
A transient invalid update preserves the last good snapshot with a degraded warning.

cases.scenario: The Agent command that launches the Dashboard exits before approval or later waves.
invariants: The detached Dashboard remains healthy and serves the exact plan identity.
Every wave and final report rechecks lifecycle status rather than trusting an earlier launch result.

cases.scenario: Applicable Codex or Claude Code instructions constrain execution.
invariants: The host-specific instruction chain controls specified fields.
The generic Graph and approval invariants remain enforced.
